liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **He's Gone** (3 reviews): Reviewer calls this probably their favorite version of the song ever; Second-set run of He's Gone, Truckin', The Other One and Eyes is singled out as unbeatable [8][11][14]
- **The Other One** (1 review, 1 other source): Goes far out before settling into a gentle, swinging Eyes of the World; Uploader notes the Other One contains a Slipknot jam [3][19]
- **Eyes Of The World** (2 reviews): Played at a slightly slower pace than usual, which the reviewer feels works very well; The jam after Eyes is tight with no flubs, bubbling up like champagne [8][19]
- **Weather Report Suite** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds the second-set Weather Report Suite solid; Reviewer rates this Weather Report Suite among the best they have heard [11][15]
- **Here Comes Sunhine** (1 review): Reviewer finds the first-set Here Comes Sunshine smoking hot [13]
- **Ship Of Fools** (1 review): Jerry brings new lead ideas to this song, one of the reviewer's highlights along with Sugaree [10]
- **Big River** (1 review): Reviewer counts this Big River among their all-time favorites [19]

## Setlist highlights

- **Save the roses, save yourselves**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **Part 1**: rare: 10 archived performances [20]
- **Winterland Concert Announcements**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1974-02-23.176226.sony.ecm250.falanga.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 32 songs; 210 min [1]
- **gd1974-02-23.sbd.miller.115607.flac16**: soundboard; 28 songs; 214 min; rated 4.82/5 by 11 [3]
- **gd74-02-23.sbd.bertha-ashley.26362.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 30 songs; 212 min; rated 4.58/5 by 38 [4]. Said about its sound: This copy is described as flawless in the remaster, with a few glitches originating in the master; Reviewer hears sound problems in the first set; Sound is nice but a little crunchy [13][15][17]
- **gd74-02-23.sbd.clugston.3382.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 29 songs; 212 min; rated 4.41/5 by 17 [5]. Said about its sound: Field recording sounds good, but vocals sit low in the mix and some song endings are cut off [10]
- **gd1974-02-23.151722.sbd.miller.flac1644**: soundboard; 28 songs; 214 min; rated 3.75/5 by 4 [6]

## Around the show

- The show ends with two and a half encores [11]
- Set II crackles with Winterland energy, and the crowd is audible on the recording [13]
- In the first set Jerry forgets some lyrics and the vocal harmonies are ragged [15]
- Reviewer says this show is often overshadowed by the following night's show [8]
- Reviewer treats the previous night, 02/22, as a warm-up and hears this show as promising for the year [10]
- Reviewer finds the Here Comes Sunshine faster than the versions played in 1973 [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1974-02-23.176226.sony.ecm250.falanga.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Louis Falanga; transferred by Bob Menke, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Louis Falanga's Master Audience Cassettes; Sony ECM 250 mic > Sony TC-110 (Maxell UD C120) [1]. Also: Charles Connor's Sony ECM 22p source supplies short patches at the starts of several songs, including Sugaree and Deal [1]
- **gd1974-02-23.sbd.miller.115607.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat [3]. Also: Matt Smith supplied the patch source; some tunings and song beginnings were patched [3]
- **gd74-02-23.sbd.bertha-ashley.26362.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [4]. Also: Reviewer credits Bertha with a remix/remaster of this soundboard, praising the work [12]
- **gd74-02-23.sbd.clugston.3382.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [5]
- **gd1974-02-23.151722.sbd.miller.flac1644**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  February 13, 2021; source: SBD > Master Reel > Dat [6]. Also: This is a corrected version of an earlier upload whose stereo channels were reversed; Joe B. Jones helped pitch-correct the patch source supplied by Matt Smith [6]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Winterland Arena - October 20, 1974](https://www.dead.net/show/october-20-1974) [21]
